title: Stripe colourwork pullover
excerpt: A drop-shoulder pullover in dk yarn worked in bold horizontal stripes. Two colours alternate in even rows across the front, back, and sleeves for a clean colourwork effect with minimal yarn management. Graded XS to 3XL.
sourceNotes: Horizontal stripe pullovers in dk weight are a popular beginner colourwork project.

glossaryTerms.definition: The point at which you switch from one yarn to the next. In stripe crochet, you complete the last stitch of a row up to the final yarn-over, then draw through the new colour to finish the stitch. This places the new colour neatly at the row edge.

Running the unused yarn loosely up the side edge of the work while the other colour is active, rather than cutting it each time. Carrying avoids multiple yarn tails at every stripe join and keeps the side seam tidy.

crochet.gaugeText: 18 dc x 20 rows = 10 x 10 cm in dk on a 4 mm hook.
crochet.finishedSizeText: Graded XS to 3XL. Size M: 104.4 cm bust.

content.text: Work back and front in horizontal stripes: 4 rows colour A, then 4 rows colour B, repeating throughout. Switch colours using a
at the end of each fourth row.
the resting yarn up the side edge to avoid cutting at every stripe. Seam shoulders. Set in sleeves. Seam sides and sleeve undersides.
Size M: 188 sts wide, 81.7 cm body. Sleeve 63.3 cm.
Chain 190. Work dc in 4-row stripes alternating A and B for 81.7 cm. Shape neck on front. Seam shoulders.
Chain 72. Work stripe sequence, increasing each end every 4 rows for 63.3 cm.
Seam sides. Work 2 rounds dc around neck in colour A.
The chevron stripe jumper adds increases and decreases to bend the stripes into a zigzag across the body.
